chapter: Rhythm and blues, the Howard Theatre and later years
title: With Ivory Joe Hunter's show in Baltimore, the Apollo and Philadelphia's Earle
summary: Phillips played show music for a month in 1951 as one of four extra men, with Dinah Washington and Mope and Pope on the bill, at the Howard, Apollo and the Earle's last show.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So when you played in those bands, did you get many solos? Or was it just mainly playing the riffs?

No, I didn't get no solos much, because I played the show. See, because he had a trumpet player in there, Little Jonesy. He used to play with Basie. He played with Don Redman, too. He was a good trumpet player. He was with him when I went with Ivory. See, I didn't stay with Ivory but about a month. I was playing shows. See, Ivory had a band that played his stuff, but I played the show music. We had four extra guys in the band that played the show with his band, in addition to what he had.
And you were in that group.
Yeah, I was in that group. We had a chick playing piano, her name was Clara Bowe.
Like that old Hollywood actress named Clara Bow.

That's right. So she was with us. He wanted musicians... He sent over here. We joined him in Baltimore. And I stayed with him in Baltimore, and I played the Howard and I played the Apollo and I played the Earle in Philadelphia. We did the last show in there; they tore it down after the show we did. Dinah Washington was on the bill with us, and Mope and Pope (that's a comedy team), and somebody else... It was a show. So we had to play... See, when we got on there, they had them arrangements to play for those people, and that little band he had couldn't cover them. Then we had a trombone player; I forgot his name. He's out of Baltimore. They called him Trummy.
